speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, can you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your eyelids, such as drooping, or any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fluctuating weakness that improves with rest is a very significant clue. Do you have any difficulty with facial movements, such as smiling or closing your eyes tightly?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further narrow down the cause, does the weakness or double vision tend to worsen later in the day or after prolonged use of the muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms improving with rest and worsening with activity is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. I will now order specific tests to confirm this suspicion. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography (Repetitive Nerve Stimulation): Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies and the decremental response on nerve stimulation confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
